messages.author: 512610f4917ceaf3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Vignette Failure
parts:
Daniel,

If RStan and Rcpp are out of sync, I think R will usually crash.

If the Stan compiler runs ok but does not recognize any input (as Michael's output shows), I believe the Stan compiler has been built with clang++ and -Ox where x > 0 and using C++11 features (default under Mavericks and newer Xcode tools).

I think Ben prevents this from happening by suggesting folks to install RStan using g++ and then switch to clang++.

Another way around this is to enforce installing with -O0, hence I asked Michael for his Makevars file.

Somehow this problem gets introduced when the RStan package is built. For quite a while I replaced the Stan part in RStan on my system and rebuild the RStan package. As I don't use RStan that often, I now simple force -O0 in my Makevars.

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Vignette Failure
parts:
The problem is that the RStan2.2 won’t work with the LLVM standard library (libc++) and instead must be
built with the GNU standard library (libstdc++).  g++ defaults to libstdc++, which is why the easiest fix
is to install RStan with g++ and then switch back to Clang for the improved model compilation.  Alternatively
one can always install using Clang but forcing -lib=libstdc++.

The conflict that’s causing RStan compilation to fail with libc++ has been fixed and will be available in
the forthcoming RStan2.3.

I think Ben prevents this from happening by suggesting folks to install RStan using g++ and then switch to clang++.

Another way around this is to enforce installing with -O0, hence I asked Michael for his Makevars file.

Somehow this problem gets introduced when the RStan package is built. For quite a while I replaced the Stan part in RStan on my system and rebuild the RStan package. As I don't use RStan that often, I now simple force -O0 in my Makevars.
